name: Iran
note: Each claim is one rendered observation on the canonical page. IDs are TL:<subject>:<measure>:<vintage> and stable across builds: a changed value under the same ID is an upstream revision (recorded in the ledger at /ledger); a new observed year is a new claim. A null or absent figure mints no claim — absence is never zero. Scheme: https://terralore.co/integrity

claims.title: The kingdom of Elam and the city of Susa
claims.summary: Elam, one of the earliest civilisations of the region, flourishes around its capital Susa in south-western Iran, trading and warring with Mesopotamia until Susa is sacked by the Assyrians around 647 BCE.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iran: From Cyrus the Great's first world empire to the Islamic Republic.", terralore.co/country/IRN/chronicle#ev-3200bce-the-kingdom-of-elam-and-the-city-of-susa, claim TL:IRN:event:3200bce:the-kingdom-of-elam-and-the-city-of-susa, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Cyrus the Great founds the Achaemenid Empire
claims.summary: Cyrus II overthrows the Median king Astyages and unites the Medes and Persians, founding the Achaemenid (Persian) Empire — the first Persian world empire.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iran: From Cyrus the Great's first world empire to the Islamic Republic.", terralore.co/country/IRN/chronicle#ev-550bce-cyrus-the-great-founds-the-achaemenid-empire, claim TL:IRN:event:550bce:cyrus-the-great-founds-the-achaemenid-empire, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Conquest of Babylon and the Cyrus Cylinder
claims.summary: Cyrus captures Babylon and issues the Cyrus Cylinder, a Babylonian cuneiform document recording his restoration of temples and return of deported peoples, often hailed as an early charter of tolerance.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iran: From Cyrus the Great's first world empire to the Islamic Republic.", terralore.co/country/IRN/chronicle#ev-539bce-conquest-of-babylon-and-the-cyrus-cylinder, claim TL:IRN:event:539bce:conquest-of-babylon-and-the-cyrus-cylinder, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Darius I builds Persepolis
claims.summary: Darius the Great organises the empire into satrapies, builds the Royal Road and standardised coinage, and begins the magnificent ceremonial capital of Persepolis, today a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iran: From Cyrus the Great's first world empire to the Islamic Republic.", terralore.co/country/IRN/chronicle#ev-518bce-darius-i-builds-persepolis, claim TL:IRN:event:518bce:darius-i-builds-persepolis, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Alexander conquers Persia and burns Persepolis
claims.summary: After defeating Darius III at Gaugamela (331 BCE), Alexander the Great enters and burns Persepolis and the last Achaemenid king is killed, ending the empire in 330 BCE.

sources.label: Alexander the Great & the Burning of Persepolis

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iran: From Cyrus the Great's first world empire to the Islamic Republic.", terralore.co/country/IRN/chronicle#ev-330bce-alexander-conquers-persia-and-burns-persepolis, claim TL:IRN:event:330bce:alexander-conquers-persia-and-burns-persepolis, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Parthian (Arsacid) Empire
claims.summary: Arsaces I founds the Parthian Empire in north-eastern Iran, reviving Persian traditions and becoming Rome's chief rival in the East for nearly five centuries.

sources.label: Ancient Iran — The Hellenistic and Parthian periods

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iran: From Cyrus the Great's first world empire to the Islamic Republic.", terralore.co/country/IRN/chronicle#ev-247bce-the-parthian-arsacid-empire, claim TL:IRN:event:247bce:the-parthian-arsacid-empire, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Ardashir I founds the Sasanian Empire
claims.summary: Ardashir I overthrows the last Parthian king and establishes the Sasanian Empire, the last great pre-Islamic Persian state, with its capital at Ctesiphon.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iran: From Cyrus the Great's first world empire to the Islamic Republic.", terralore.co/country/IRN/chronicle#ev-224-ardashir-i-founds-the-sasanian-empire, claim TL:IRN:event:224:ardashir-i-founds-the-sasanian-empire, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Zoroastrianism as state religion
claims.summary: The Sasanian kings establish Zoroastrianism, the faith attributed to the prophet Zoroaster, as the official religion of Iran, supported by a powerful priesthood and network of fire temples.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iran: From Cyrus the Great's first world empire to the Islamic Republic.", terralore.co/country/IRN/chronicle#ev-224-zoroastrianism-as-state-religion, claim TL:IRN:event:224:zoroastrianism-as-state-religion, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Exhausting wars with Byzantium
claims.summary: The last great Byzantine–Sasanian war drains both empires militarily and economically, leaving Persia dangerously weakened on the eve of the Arab conquest.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iran: From Cyrus the Great's first world empire to the Islamic Republic.", terralore.co/country/IRN/chronicle#ev-628-exhausting-wars-with-byzantium, claim TL:IRN:event:628:exhausting-wars-with-byzantium, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Battle of Nahavand — the 'Victory of Victories'
claims.summary: Arab Muslim forces crush the Sasanian army at Nahavand, breaking organised Persian resistance; the empire finally collapses with the death of Yazdegerd III in 651 CE.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iran: From Cyrus the Great's first world empire to the Islamic Republic.", terralore.co/country/IRN/chronicle#ev-642-battle-of-nahavand-the-victory-of-victories, claim TL:IRN:event:642:battle-of-nahavand-the-victory-of-victories, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Islamisation of Persia begins
claims.summary: With the Sasanian state destroyed, Iran is incorporated into the Islamic caliphate; over the following centuries most of its people convert to Islam while retaining the Persian language and much of their culture.

sources.label: The Phases, History, and Legacy of the Arab Conquests (632–750 CE)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iran: From Cyrus the Great's first world empire to the Islamic Republic.", terralore.co/country/IRN/chronicle#ev-651-islamisation-of-persia-begins, claim TL:IRN:event:651:islamisation-of-persia-begins, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Abbasid Revolution and the rise of Baghdad
claims.summary: Backed by support from Persian Khorasan, the Abbasids overthrow the Umayyads and found Baghdad, drawing heavily on Persian administrative and intellectual traditions.

sources.label: The Phases, History, and Legacy of the Arab Conquests (632–750 CE)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iran: From Cyrus the Great's first world empire to the Islamic Republic.", terralore.co/country/IRN/chronicle#ev-750-abbasid-revolution-and-the-rise-of-baghdad, claim TL:IRN:event:750:abbasid-revolution-and-the-rise-of-baghdad, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Persia at the heart of the Islamic golden age
claims.summary: In the House of Wisdom and beyond, Persian scholars such as Avicenna, al-Khwarizmi and Omar Khayyam advance medicine, mathematics and astronomy during the Islamic golden age.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iran: From Cyrus the Great's first world empire to the Islamic Republic.", terralore.co/country/IRN/chronicle#ev-1000-persia-at-the-heart-of-the-islamic-golden-age, claim TL:IRN:event:1000:persia-at-the-heart-of-the-islamic-golden-age, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Ferdowsi completes the Shahnameh
claims.summary: The poet Ferdowsi finishes the Shahnameh, the 'Book of Kings', an epic of some 50,000 couplets that preserves Iran's mythic and pre-Islamic history and anchors the Persian language.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iran: From Cyrus the Great's first world empire to the Islamic Republic.", terralore.co/country/IRN/chronicle#ev-1010-ferdowsi-completes-the-shahnameh, claim TL:IRN:event:1010:ferdowsi-completes-the-shahnameh, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Mongol invasion of Iran
claims.summary: Genghis Khan's armies invade Iran, devastating its cities; his grandson Hulagu completes the conquest, taking Alamut in 1256 and destroying Baghdad in 1258, and founds the Ilkhanate.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iran: From Cyrus the Great's first world empire to the Islamic Republic.", terralore.co/country/IRN/chronicle#ev-1219-mongol-invasion-of-iran, claim TL:IRN:event:1219:mongol-invasion-of-iran, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Timur and the Timurid era
claims.summary: Timur (Tamerlane) conquers the lands of the former Ilkhanate, founding the Timurid empire whose courts become celebrated centres of Persianate art and learning.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iran: From Cyrus the Great's first world empire to the Islamic Republic.", terralore.co/country/IRN/chronicle#ev-1370-timur-and-the-timurid-era, claim TL:IRN:event:1370:timur-and-the-timurid-era, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Ismail I founds the Safavid dynasty and Shia Iran
claims.summary: Ismail I captures Tabriz, proclaims himself shah, and declares Twelver Shia Islam the state religion, setting Iran apart from its Sunni neighbours and shaping its identity to the present day.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iran: From Cyrus the Great's first world empire to the Islamic Republic.", terralore.co/country/IRN/chronicle#ev-1501-ismail-i-founds-the-safavid-dynasty-and-shia, claim TL:IRN:event:1501:ismail-i-founds-the-safavid-dynasty-and-shia, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Shah Abbas moves the capital to Isfahan
claims.summary: At the height of Safavid power, Shah Abbas the Great relocates the capital to Isfahan and builds the grand Naqsh-e Jahan (Imam) Square, a UNESCO World Heritage masterpiece of urban design.

sources.label: Meidan Emam, Esfahan — UNESCO World Heritage List

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iran: From Cyrus the Great's first world empire to the Islamic Republic.", terralore.co/country/IRN/chronicle#ev-1598-shah-abbas-moves-the-capital-to-isfahan, claim TL:IRN:event:1598:shah-abbas-moves-the-capital-to-isfahan, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Afghan sack of Isfahan and Safavid decline
claims.summary: Afghan invaders besiege and sack Isfahan, shattering Safavid power; the dynasty formally ends in 1736, opening a period of instability before the rise of the Qajars.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iran: From Cyrus the Great's first world empire to the Islamic Republic.", terralore.co/country/IRN/chronicle#ev-1722-afghan-sack-of-isfahan-and-safavid-decline, claim TL:IRN:event:1722:afghan-sack-of-isfahan-and-safavid-decline, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Persian Constitutional Revolution
claims.summary: After mass protests, Mozaffar al-Din Shah grants a constitution and the first Majles (parliament), a pioneering experiment in constitutional government in the Middle East.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iran: From Cyrus the Great's first world empire to the Islamic Republic.", terralore.co/country/IRN/chronicle#ev-1906-persian-constitutional-revolution, claim TL:IRN:event:1906:persian-constitutional-revolution, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Discovery of oil
claims.summary: Oil is struck in south-western Iran, making the country a strategic prize and tying its economy to foreign-controlled concessions for decades to come.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iran: From Cyrus the Great's first world empire to the Islamic Republic.", terralore.co/country/IRN/chronicle#ev-1908-discovery-of-oil, claim TL:IRN:event:1908:discovery-of-oil, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Reza Khan founds the Pahlavi dynasty
claims.summary: Having seized power in a 1921 coup, Reza Khan deposes the last Qajar shah and is crowned Reza Shah Pahlavi, launching an authoritarian drive to modernise and centralise Iran.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iran: From Cyrus the Great's first world empire to the Islamic Republic.", terralore.co/country/IRN/chronicle#ev-1925-reza-khan-founds-the-pahlavi-dynasty, claim TL:IRN:event:1925:reza-khan-founds-the-pahlavi-dynasty, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The CIA-backed coup against Mosaddegh
claims.summary: Prime Minister Mohammad Mosaddegh, who had nationalised the oil industry, is overthrown in August 1953 in a coup organised by the CIA and British intelligence, restoring the shah's power.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iran: From Cyrus the Great's first world empire to the Islamic Republic.", terralore.co/country/IRN/chronicle#ev-1953-the-cia-backed-coup-against-mosaddegh, claim TL:IRN:event:1953:the-cia-backed-coup-against-mosaddegh, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Islamic Revolution
claims.summary: The shah flees in January 1979 and Ayatollah Khomeini returns from exile; the monarchy collapses on 11 February, ending some 2,500 years of Iranian kingship.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iran: From Cyrus the Great's first world empire to the Islamic Republic.", terralore.co/country/IRN/chronicle#ev-1979-the-islamic-revolution, claim TL:IRN:event:1979:the-islamic-revolution, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Proclamation of the Islamic Republic
claims.summary: After a referendum on 30–31 March approves the change by an overwhelming majority, Khomeini proclaims the Islamic Republic of Iran on 1 April 1979.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iran: From Cyrus the Great's first world empire to the Islamic Republic.", terralore.co/country/IRN/chronicle#ev-1979-proclamation-of-the-islamic-republic, claim TL:IRN:event:1979:proclamation-of-the-islamic-republic, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: US embassy seized and hostage crisis
claims.summary: Militant students storm the US embassy in Tehran, holding 52 Americans for 444 days and setting the new republic on a long course of confrontation with the West.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iran: From Cyrus the Great's first world empire to the Islamic Republic.", terralore.co/country/IRN/chronicle#ev-1979-us-embassy-seized-and-hostage-crisis, claim TL:IRN:event:1979:us-embassy-seized-and-hostage-crisis, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Iran–Iraq War
claims.summary: Iraq invades in September 1980, igniting a devastating eight-year war; Iran accepts UN Security Council Resolution 598 and a ceasefire takes effect on 20 August 1988.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iran: From Cyrus the Great's first world empire to the Islamic Republic.", terralore.co/country/IRN/chronicle#ev-1980-the-iran-iraq-war, claim TL:IRN:event:1980:the-iran-iraq-war, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.
